examples.question_text: A parcel is weighed as $24$ kg. Find the percentage error, correct to two decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
The precision is $1$ kg.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Absolute error}&=\tfrac12\times1\\&=0.5\text{ kg}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage error}&=\frac{0.5}{24}\times100\%\\&\approx2.08\%\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Find the percentage error of each measurement, correct to three decimal places.
(a) $4.25$ kg
(b) $36.0$ s, correct to one decimal place
examples.solution_text:
(a) The precision is $0.01$ kg.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Absolute error}&=\tfrac12\times0.01\\&=0.005\text{ kg}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage error}&=\frac{0.005}{4.25}\times100\%\\&\approx0.118\%\end{aligned}$
(b) The trailing zero records tenths of a second, so the precision is $0.1$ s.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Absolute error}&=\tfrac12\times0.1\\&=0.05\text{ s}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage error}&=\frac{0.05}{36.0}\times100\%\\&\approx0.139\%\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Find the percentage error of each measurement, correct to two decimal places.
(a) A road measured as $650$ m, to the nearest $10$ m
(b) A ribbon measured as $17.0$ cm, to the nearest $0.5$ cm
examples.solution_text:
(a) The stated precision is $10$ m.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Absolute error}&=\tfrac12\times10\\&=5\text{ m}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage error}&=\frac{5}{650}\times100\%\\&\approx0.77\%\end{aligned}$
(b) The stated precision is $0.5$ cm.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Absolute error}&=\tfrac12\times0.5\\&=0.25\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage error}&=\frac{0.25}{17.0}\times100\%\\&\approx1.47\%\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A container's capacity is measured as $1.85$ L, correct to the nearest $10$ mL. Find the percentage error, correct to two decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
The precision is $10$ mL.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Absolute error}&=\tfrac12\times10\\&=5\text{ mL}\end{aligned}$
Convert the measurement to millilitres before dividing.
$\begin{aligned}1.85\text{ L}&=1.85\times1000\text{ mL}\\&=1850\text{ mL}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage error}&=\frac{5}{1850}\times100\%\\&\approx0.27\%\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: An object is weighed as $20$ kg and then as $20.3$ kg using a more precise scale. Calculate each percentage error, correct to two decimal places, and explain why the second is smaller.
examples.solution_text:
For $20$ kg, the precision is $1$ kg.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Absolute error}&=\tfrac12\times1\\&=0.5\text{ kg}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage error}&=\frac{0.5}{20}\times100\%\\&=2.50\%\end{aligned}$
For $20.3$ kg, the precision is $0.1$ kg.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Absolute error}&=\tfrac12\times0.1\\&=0.05\text{ kg}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage error}&=\frac{0.05}{20.3}\times100\%\\&\approx0.25\%\end{aligned}$
The measurements are nearly the same size. The second absolute error is ten times smaller, giving a much smaller percentage error.

examples.derivation: Precision 1 kg gives absolute error 0.5 kg. (0.5/24) × 100% = 2.083333…%, which rounds to 2.08%.

(a) Precision 0.01 kg gives absolute error 0.005 kg; (0.005/4.25) × 100% = 0.117647…%, rounding to 0.118%. (b) The stated decimal place gives precision 0.1 s and absolute error 0.05 s; (0.05/36.0) × 100% = 0.138888…%, rounding to 0.139%.

(a) Stated precision 10 m gives absolute error 5 m; (5/650) × 100% = 0.769230…%, rounding to 0.77%. (b) Stated precision 0.5 cm overrides the displayed decimal precision and gives absolute error 0.25 cm; (0.25/17.0) × 100% = 1.470588…%, rounding to 1.47%.
Precision 10 mL gives absolute error 5 mL. Convert 1.85 L to 1850 mL; (5/1850) × 100% = 0.270270…%, rounding to 0.27%.

For 20 kg, absolute error is 0.5 kg and percentage error is 2.50%. For 20.3 kg, absolute error is 0.05 kg; (0.05/20.3) × 100% = 0.246305…%, rounding to 0.25%. The measurements are approximately equal, while the second absolute error is ten times smaller, supporting the explanation.
